newsitem.title: UK: Guinness posts higher profits, sees encouraging signs.
newsitem.headline: Guinness posts higher profits, sees encouraging signs.

text.p: Guinness Plc posted an 11 percent rise in 1996 pretax profits to 975 million pounds ($1.56 billion) Thursday, aided by strength of its distilled spirits.
"We have seen in developed markets, and particularly in the United States, the start of a turnaround, for the first time since the early 1980's," said Chairman Tony Greener.

Sales volumes at United Distillers (UD), the company's spirits arm, rose 1 percent in 1996 to 45.7 million cases, an increase of 0.6 million on 1995. UD achieved an overall average price increase in the year of around 1.5 percent and Greener made positive remarks about the climate for pricing in the coming year.
"Going forward our feeling is the climate for pricing is improving and in terms of Scotch (whisky) volume we would expect to see the underlying rate of growth on Scotch sales improving again."
Greener said the company had already announced a number of price increases for the coming year, "Our sense is the overall climate for price increases will be somewhat more favourable this year."
Scotch whisky sales at 25.7 million cases were 1 percent below the comparable 1995 level due to deliberately reduced shipments designed to reduce trade stock levels.
"Sales of Johnnie Walker Black Label were up by 6 percent. So we are really seeing a good strong performance at consumer level in the States which I really think is encouraging," he said.
The company has announced a 2 percent price rise in the United States, due to come into effect on July 1.
"The U.S economy, being strong, is very helpful although in Europe, progress remains slow and we do not expect a big consumer bounceback in Germany and France," Greener said.
